title: Stored XSS through bot names or account names in the dashboard
description: Bot names and e-mail addresses are rendered in the new switcher and account card.
reason: All values are HTML-escaped or set as textContent; names are also stripped of <, > and newlines on the server; CSP limits script sources.

title: CSRF against the account and bot admin APIs

trace.description: Credentials come only from the Authorization header.

evidence.description: No cookies are issued; tokens live in sessionStorage and are sent explicitly.

reason: Without ambient credentials a cross-site page cannot authenticate; /api/auth/* and /api/admin/* send no CORS headers, so cross-origin reads are also blocked.

title: CPU exhaustion through password hashing on sign-in

evidence.description: if (await loginLocked(c, scope)) return 429 — before verifyLogin()

reason: Hashing costs ~5 ms per attempt and only 8 failed attempts per IP per 10 minutes reach it; each request is its own Worker invocation, so there is no shared CPU to exhaust.

title: Anyone can register someone else's e-mail address
description: Sign-up does not verify e-mail ownership, so an attacker can register a victim's address first; the victim then gets 409 until the squatted account expires after 7 days.
root_cause: No e-mail ownership proof before creating the account.
intended_behavior: Only the owner of an e-mail address can create an account for it.

trace.description: Account bound to an unverified e-mail.

evidence.description: Second sign-up with the same e-mail gets 409

conditions.description: Attacker knows the victim's e-mail and signs up first.

instructions: Sign up with an address you do not own; the real owner's sign-up then returns 409.

remediation.strategy: Accepted for now: accounts expire after 7 days and hold no data of the victim. Proper fix: e-mail verification link (Cloudflare Email Routing / an e-mail API) before activation.

likelihood.reason: Targeted, needs the victim's address in advance.

impact.reason: Delays the victim's sign-up by up to 7 days; no access to the victim's data.

title: Suggestion regeneration called the AI without any limit
description: POST /api/admin/suggestions/regenerate ran generateSuggestions (an LLM call) on every request with no rate limit or quota, so an owner could loop it to spend shared AI budget.
root_cause: An AI-spending admin action was not metered.
intended_behavior: Regeneration is rate-limited per bot and counted in the user bot's daily quota.

trace.description: LLM call through the bot's chain.

evidence.description: Fixed: allow(`regen:${bot}`, 3) per minute and dailyQuota('owner-regen', 20, ...) for user bots

conditions.description: Any self-registered account with an indexed document.

instructions: Reason from source: no limiter before the AI call.
execution.observed_result: Source-confirmed; now returns 429 after 3 calls per minute.

remediation.strategy: Per-bot rate limit plus daily quota before the AI call.

code_changes.fixed_code: if (!allow(`regen:${bot}`, 3)) return 429; if (bot !== DEFAULT_BOT && !(await dailyQuota(...))) return 429;

impact.reason: Bounded by the per-isolate rate and the platform daily total.

title: User bots could run any Workers AI model on the platform's account
description: normalizeSettings accepts any model string for the 'workers-ai' provider, and openStream/completeChat passed it straight to env.AI.run. A free account could configure a much larger model (for example a 70B model) for its bot and its owner tests, multiplying the neurons each question costs on the shared platform account.
root_cause: The model id for the platform-paid provider was owner-controlled with no allow-list at the call site.
intended_behavior: User bots may only call the allow-listed Workers AI chat models; other providers use the owner's own keys.

trace.description: Owner saves settings.chain with provider 'workers-ai' and any model.
Model string kept as is (only length-limited).

evidence.description: Fixed: assertWorkersAiModel() rejects non-allow-listed models when env.TENANT_BOT is set

instructions: Run the Worker locally, sign in as a seeded user and test a large Workers AI model.
execution.observed_result: After the fix the call is refused before env.AI.run with 'tidak tersedia untuk bot pengguna' (Playwright: 'user bots cannot pick expensive Workers AI models').

remediation.strategy: Mark tenant environments (tenantEnv sets TENANT_BOT) and enforce the Workers AI model allow-list right before every env.AI.run chat call.

code_changes.fixed_code: if (env.TENANT_BOT && model !== WORKERS_AI_PRIMARY && model !== WORKERS_AI_BACKUP) throw { status: 403, ... }

likelihood.reason: Sign-up is open; the setting is reachable through the documented config API.

impact.reason: Faster exhaustion of the shared AI allowance for every tenant; no data exposure.

confidence.reason: Direct source path; fix covered by a local Worker test.
